To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stray microwaves can be a significant source of systematic error in the NIST-F1 primary frequency standard, and that this error is measurable and can be reduced.

the frequency of the primary frequency standard can be affected by stray microwave leakage fields, that these fields can be measured, that their effect is linear in the power, and that the leakage can be used to locate the position of the atoms in the standard.

the frequency shift of a primary standard due to stray microwaves is proportional to the square root of the stray microwave power, and is proportional to the stray magnetic field at the location where the atoms are released from the fountain.

the development of a novel technique to measure microwave leakage-induced frequency shifts of the atomic fountain frequency standards NIST-F1 at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and IEN-CSFI at the Istituto Elettronica Nazionale, Italy.

the measurement of the frequency of a microwave signal, which is the basis of all time and frequency standards, and the determination of the frequency stability of the signal source used to generate the signal to be measured.
the development of new techniques for the measurement of microwave leakage-induced frequency shifts.

the stray microwave leakage in the primary standards NIST-F1 (and IEN-CSF 1) is small, and that it is not the dominant source of systematic error in either primary standard.
stray microwave fields in the Ramsey cavities of the primary frequency standards NIST-F1, NIST-F2, and IEN-CSFI can shift the central Ramsey fringe frequency by as much as 1.4 Hz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stray fields are a significant source of frequency shifts in atomic fountain standards.

the frequency shift due to the stray microwave fields is a function of the power in the stray field, the frequency of the stray field, and the frequency of the standard, but not of the phase of the stray field.
the microwave leakage-induced frequency shift in the primary frequency standards NIST-F1, NIST-F2 and IEN-CSf 1 can be measured and even the location of the leakage source determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stray microwave fields are due to leakage from the cavity and can be measured by varying the cavity power and measuring the frequency shift.
the stray fields are not random, but instead have a systematic component that can be exploited.
the microwave leakage fields in these standards are not negligible, and that the frequency shifts they cause can be measured.
